title: Deduction and Credit Entries on Payout Methods Ledgers
content:
Each deduction and each credit on a Payout Methods ledger carries the record that created it, and its amount is set by that record.

## Deductions (amounts the host owes)

| Kind of deduction | Amount |
|---|---|
| Refund clawback | The host-funded guest refunds issued after the payout release on the stay, less the host service fee refunded on them |
| Cancellation penalty | The penalty charged |
| Protection premium | The premium charged on the stay |
| Guest payment reversal | The guest damage payment reversed |

## Credits (amounts owed to the host)

| Kind of credit | Amount |
|---|---|
| Claim reimbursement | The reimbursement paid on the claim |
| Guest damage payment | The guest payment recorded |
| Penalty waiver | The penalty waived |
| Premium refund | The premium refunded |

## Booking rule for credits

A credit is booked once per source record and never netted against a deduction; both are booked in full and the balance shows the net. Where the payout ledger already shows a credit of the same kind naming the same source record, no second credit is booked for it.

## Hypothetical example

An imagined host is charged a USD 210.00 cancellation penalty and later wins a waiver of the same USD 210.00. The ledger shows a USD 210.00 cancellation-penalty deduction and, separately, a USD 210.00 penalty-waiver credit; the two are not netted into a single zero entry, and the balance shows the net of both.

An imagined guest receives USD 400.00 in host-funded refunds after the payout release on a stay, on which USD 12.00 of host service fee is refunded. The refund clawback is USD 400.00 less USD 12.00, that is USD 388.00.
